title: Jin dynasty frontier trenches (Jin jiehao)
summary: The Jurchen Jin dynasty built a long frontier system of earth walls and deep ditches across what are now Inner Mongolia, Hebei, Jilin and Heilongjiang to slow steppe cavalry. Construction began in 1123 and reached its final form around 1198, but did not stop the Mongol invasions.

uncertainty.note: Global Times (2026) gives 1123 as the start and about 1198 as the final form; another outlet describes an early-Jin northern line and a late-Jin southern line without years. Length estimates conflict (4,500 km to 6,500 km).

where.modern_name: Hexigten Banner, Chifeng, Inner Mongolia, China (2025 survey area; the system spans Inner Mongolia, Hebei, Jilin and Heilongjiang)
where.historical_name: Frontier of the Jin dynasty (Jurchen), facing the Mongols

importance.justification: A very large medieval frontier defense system of north China built around trenches.

sources.title: Chinese archaeologists identify 20 new features of the Jin Great Wall in Inner Mongolia
Heilongjiang Province: the Jin Boundary Trench

reviewer_note: Least sure of dates and extent: Global Times gives 1123-1198, another page only early and late Jin, and lengths run 4,500-6,500 km. The Global Times headline is my paraphrase. The pin is one surveyed segment, not the whole system; the id suggests c. 1150 but no opened source gives that year.
